nodes.summary: The proposition that for every real number $C > 0$ there is a natural number $K \ge 3$ such that there are infinitely many triples $(a, b, n)$ of positive integers with $a + b > n + C \log n$ for which no prime $p > K$ divides the denominator of the rational number $n! / (a! \, b!)$ in lowest terms.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 729

nodes.summary: For every real number $C > 0$ there is a natural number $K \ge 3$ such that there are infinitely many triples $(a, b, n)$ of positive integers with $a + b > n + C \log n$ for which no prime $p > K$ divides the denominator of the rational number $n! / (a! \, b!)$ in lowest terms.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 729 holds

nodes.summary: There is a real number $\delta > 0$ such that for every real number $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon < \delta$ and all real numbers $C > 0$ and $C' > C$, there are natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n \ge 1$ with $a > \varepsilon n$, $b > \varepsilon n$, $a! \, b! \mid n! \, (a + b - n)!$ and $n + C \log n < a + b < n + C' \log n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 728 holds

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a real number $\delta > 0$ such that for every real number $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon < \delta$ and all real numbers $C > 0$ and $C' > C$, there are natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n \ge 1$ with $a > \varepsilon n$, $b > \varepsilon n$, $a! \, b! \mid n! \, (a + b - n)!$ and $n + C \log n < a + b < n + C' \log n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 728

nodes.summary: For all lists $A$ and $B$ of natural numbers, $\prod_{b \in B} (b \cdot 0)!$ divides $\prod_{a \in A} (a \cdot 0)!$, since both products equal $1$.
nodes.title: Scaled factorial products at index zero divide

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of natural numbers, $\prod_{a \in L} (a \cdot 0)! = 1$, since every factor equals $0! = 1$.
nodes.title: Scaled factorial product at index zero

nodes.summary: For a list $L$ of natural numbers and a natural number $n$, the product of scaled factorials of $L$ at $n$ is $\prod_{a \in L} (an)!$, the product of the factorials $(an)!$ over the entries $a$ of $L$, counted with multiplicity; for the empty list it is $1$.
nodes.title: Product of scaled factorials

nodes.summary: The tuples $(2)$ and $(1, 1)$ form an integral factorial ratio: their entries are positive, their sums agree ($2 = 1 + 1$), and for every natural number $n$, $n! \cdot n!$ divides $(2n)!$.
nodes.title: The central binomial factorial ratio is integral

nodes.summary: For lists $A$ and $B$ of natural numbers, $(A, B)$ is an integral factorial ratio if and only if every entry of $A$ is positive, every entry of $B$ is positive, the entries of $A$ and the entries of $B$ have the same sum, and for every natural number $n$ the product $\prod_{b \in B} (bn)!$ divides $\prod_{a \in A} (an)!$.
nodes.title: Characterization of integral factorial ratios

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $A'$ and $B$ be lists of natural numbers such that $A'$ is a permutation of $A$. If $(A, B)$ is an integral factorial ratio, then so is $(A', B)$.
nodes.title: Permuting the numerator of an integral factorial ratio

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$ and $B'$ be lists of natural numbers such that $B'$ is a permutation of $B$. If $(A, B)$ is an integral factorial ratio, then so is $(A, B')$.
nodes.title: Permuting the denominator of an integral factorial ratio

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $A'$, $B$ and $B'$ be lists of natural numbers such that $A'$ is a permutation of $A$ and $B'$ is a permutation of $B$. If $(A, B)$ is an integral factorial ratio, then so is $(A', B')$.
nodes.title: Integral factorial ratios are invariant under permutation

nodes.summary: If every entry of a list $L$ of natural numbers is positive, then $(L, L)$ is an integral factorial ratio.
nodes.title: Equal tuples form an integral factorial ratio

nodes.summary: For every positive natural number $c$, the one-entry tuples $(c)$ and $(c)$ form an integral factorial ratio.
nodes.title: Equal singletons form an integral factorial ratio

nodes.summary: For lists $A = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$ and $B = (b_1, \dots, b_l)$ of natural numbers, the pair $(A, B)$ is an integral factorial ratio when every $a_i$ and every $b_j$ is positive, $a_1 + \dots + a_k = b_1 + \dots + b_l$, and for every natural number $n$ the product $(b_1 n)! \cdots (b_l n)!$ divides $(a_1 n)! \cdots (a_k n)!$; equivalently, the quotient $\frac{(a_1 n)! \cdots (a_k n)!}{(b_1 n)! \cdots (b_l n)!}$ is a…
nodes.title: Integral factorial ratio

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
